Work playbook — change 0001-billing-invoice-export — agent-executed (ADR 0005).

Prompt: "add a billing invoice export"
Likely capabilities (deterministic term match — a hint, not a decision):
    billing              score 110   .doctrina/specs/billing/spec.md

Execute in order, in a single linear pass:

1. Read the context pack and confirm (or correct) the capability:
       doctrina context billing --concat

2. If the capability has no spec yet:
       doctrina spec new <capability>
   Trace it to product intent: tag the product.md success-criteria bullet
   it serves with an anchor ("- [SC1] ...") and set the spec's
   "**Realizes:** SC1" header (or "n/a — <why>"). `doctrina validate` warns
   on an active spec with no Realizes; `doctrina trace` reports the link.

3. A delta is already scaffolded (Operation prefilled) at
   .doctrina/changes/0001-billing-invoice-export/specs/billing/delta.md — fill its body.
   It was RANKED, not pinned — confirm the capability first; the file
   says how to correct it if the ranking got it wrong.
   Add one more delta per additional affected capability:
       # Spec Delta — capability: <capability>
       **Operation:** ADDED | MODIFIED | REMOVED
       **Target spec on apply:** `.doctrina/specs/<capability>/spec.md`
       ---
       <EARS body. Keep the two axes honest (Status vs Implementation),
        keep aspiration under ## Maturity → Future, and cite the proof per
        criterion: "1. [unverified] <signal> — verified by `path/to/test`">
   New capability? `spec new` then an ADDED delta with the FULL body — apply
   replaces the untouched scaffold. Bookkeeping edits? MODIFIED with an ops
   block, applied mechanically (all ops or none):
       ```ops
       set-header Implementation: verified — `src/x.js`
       bump-version minor
       set-criterion 1: verified
       append-criterion [unverified] new signal — verified by `test/y.test.js`
       append-requirement event: When <trigger>, the system shall <action>.
       replace-requirement ubiquitous 2: The system shall <action>.
       ```
   append-* ops number/position at APPLY time, so concurrent changes
   appending to the same spec never collide. Only free-prose rewrites
   (Purpose, Maturity, ...) stay a by-hand merge.

4. Replace the placeholder tasks in .doctrina/changes/0001-billing-invoice-export/tasks.md
   with small, checkable implementation tasks (a few hours each, max),
   and record the change's What/Scope in its proposal.md. Do this BEFORE
   implementing — analyze and close refuse a change whose scaffold
   placeholders were never replaced, and `change tick` will not tick them.

5. Implement task by task, checking each box as it lands. Advance the
   spec's Implementation: planned → partial → implemented as code lands.
   If the prompt is genuinely ambiguous, ask the user before assuming.

6. ADR checkpoint — does this change decide something structural
   (an architecture, a boundary, a trade-off a future session must
   not relitigate)? If yes: doctrina decision new "<title>" now,
   before closing — the definition of done requires it recorded.
   (close re-checks this: it warns when the change touches capabilities
   cited by an accepted ADR — amend via decision supersede, not silence.)
   Touching an integration surface (ports, env vars, public endpoints)?
   Own it in a contract: doctrina contract new <id> · doctrina contract check.

7. Close in one attested pass (preferred — runs every gate and stops
   at the first failure with the exact rerun command):
       doctrina close 0001-billing-invoice-export
   It self-reviews on the way through: the close runs `doctrina review`
   before the apply, where its findings can still change what gets
   written. Advisory — it reports and the close continues.
   The sequence is declared in one place and printed by the close itself,
   so read it there rather than from a copy that goes stale.
   Before it: check the proposal's ## Verification boxes and every task,
   closing steps included, and bump Implementation to verified.
   Two gates ask for WRITING, and both refuse late if you leave them:
   a change that alters a documented surface needs the documentation to
   move with it, AND an entry in the project's changelog — one says how it
   works, the other says that it changed. If the command and flag names in
   your prose are only MENTIONED, declare it instead of forcing:
   - **Documented surface:** n/a — <why> in the proposal.

8. doctrina next for the follow-up.
   If this change taught a reusable lesson (a fix you'd hate to relearn,
   a recurring convention), capture it: doctrina skill new <slug>.
